Nest is in a  live birch tree, bottom of canopy, betweent he tertiary road and the water (water hardly seen from vantage), nest almost parallel with road as it begins to slope down towards the water. Osprey required to fly up through the tree canopies to exit and enter nest. No signs of fish bones, tails, skin, or scale as characteristic of an active nest. No signs of occupancy at time of site visit. Nest in very goon condition, looks more like raven nest, perhaps taken over by Osprey. Other suitable platform type poplar trees in area that look as though they would make ideal Osprey nest locations.
